➕ Record a Bill

For a sale that didn't go through the 🛒 Sales Counter cart — a quick informal sale, a service billed later, etc. This doesn't touch inventory quantities.

🕓 Record a Past Sale

For a sale that actually happened but never got entered at the time — no power, phone/laptop wasn't handy, or it was just missed. This deducts stock and adds it to revenue for the date/time you choose, exactly like a normal sale.

🕓 Record a Past Hire

For a hire that actually went out but never got entered at the time. This reduces available stock (or marks a unit as hired) and adds it to Hires exactly like a normal hire, just backdated to the date/time you choose.

Still counted as out on hire from the date above — held-so-far and amount owed are calculated the same way as any other Count As You Go hire, right up to today.

👤 Client Information

Leave the amount at 0.00 if nothing was collected yet (e.g. it's a Bill/Deposit-only situation) — it can be settled later from 🔄 Hires.

➕ Sell Unlisted Item

For something you don't stock — e.g. a customer needs an item you're out of, so you get it from another shop (not one of your branches) and sell it on. This adds it to the cart at the price you set; it never touches your own inventory.

🏭 Build an Item

Define a finished item's recipe — e.g. a battery built from cells, a casing, and acid. This never deducts any component stock by itself: it just declares what the item is made of. Components are only ever deducted the moment a unit actually sells or gets hired out — stock stays exactly as it is until then.

Not in inventory yet? Give it a name and it'll be added.

🔨 Assemble an Item

For an item you already stock — or a new one — define what it's built from — e.g. a battery from cells, a casing, and acid — then assemble a batch whenever you like. Unlike Production, this actually deducts the components right now and adds the finished units to this item's own stock count, permanently. Selling the finished item afterward is then just a normal sale — no components are touched again at that point.

📦 Define a Set

A Set is a named combination of separate items already in your inventory — e.g. a "Camping Kit" made of a tent, 4 chairs, and a cooler. A Set never carries its own stock: its availability is always worked out live from whatever's left of its components, and nothing is deducted until the Set itself is actually sold or hired out — at which point every component in it is deducted for real, and the receipt shows exactly what was used.

↩️ Returned Goods

Record a customer returning an item — with or without their receipt. An item returned in good condition, from a sale made at this shop, goes straight back into stock; anything damaged, or facilitated from another branch, doesn't. Exchanges are preferred and cash is never refunded — a cheaper replacement always shows KES 0.00 due, with any difference held as store credit rather than paid out.

What's happening to this item?

Top-Up (optional)

If the customer is paying extra — for an upgrade, or to have the item fixed — record it here. It's added to today's revenue like any other payment.

Return Credit

What the returned item is worth toward the exchange. Defaults to its current selling price × quantity — adjust if the agreed credit is different.

Can't find what the customer wants right now? Log the return anyway, hold their credit, and this'll remind you (and text the customer) the moment it's back in stock or the date below arrives.

Needs the customer's phone number above to send SMS reminders.

Top-Up Owed

The replacement is worth more than the return credit — collect the difference.

Store Credit Issued

The return credit is worth more than the replacement. No cash is refunded — the difference (shown as KES 0.00 due below) is held as store credit on the customer's account for their next visit. Add their phone number above so it's saved correctly.

🏨 Business Details

The shop name appears in the header, at the top of every receipt and bill, and on printed reports. Changing it here updates it on every device that syncs with this shop.

🖼️ Auto Product Images

When you add a new item or service with no photo of your own, this fetches a stock photo of it automatically — only while the device is online, and only ever a fallback (your own uploaded/captured photo always wins if you add one). Uses Pixabay's free image API — get a free key at pixabay.com (Account → API).

✅ Auto product images are on.

📸 AI Capture List

Powers the "📸 Capture List" button on Add New Items and Restock — photograph or upload an invoice, handwritten note, or delivery sheet, and it reads out item names, quantities, and costs automatically, even with no column headers. Works out of the box using the platform's shared Gemini key pool — hitting its limits often, or want your own quota? Add up to 2 of your own free Google Gemini API keys below; this device tries those first, in order, before falling back to the platform pool.

✅ AI Capture List is available.

🖼️ Sales Counter Photo Grid

Shows a scrollable grid of your best-selling items below the search bar — tapping a card adds it to the cart directly. Ranked by total sales (highest first); items without a photo still show as a plain text card.

Show the photo grid

🔔 Bill Notifications

Who gets alerted on the 🔔 bell icon when a bill is created, comes due, goes overdue, or gets paid. The owner/admin (no staff checked in) always sees every alert, whether or not they're ticked below — this list is for which staff also get them.

👑 Admin / Owner

Your name shows as the default server in the header whenever no staff member is checked in.

🔢 Quantity Display

How amounts of kg / litres / metres / inches / feet (in ingredients and items) are shown — in Inventory, the Sales Counter, receipts, and reports. This is display only; whole "pcs" items are never affected.

🔥 Gas Refill & Sales

Turn this on if you sell/refill LPG gas cylinders. Adds a 🔥 Gas Refill tab (right after 🛒 Sales Counter) where you register cylinder brands/weights and accessories, then take Refill/Exchange, Complete Set, and Outright sales — each cylinder variant tracks Full and Empty stock separately.

🧾 VAT / Tax

Prices already include VAT. Every item is assigned a bracket when it's added (Inventory tab lets you change it any time) — receipts always show the tax breakdown, computed per item.

🔔 Alert Notifications

Get a notification on this device when an item runs low or nears its expiry date — instead of only finding out when you open the 🔔 bell menu. Each item is announced once per day. This is a per-device setting: turn it on wherever you want to be alerted.

Off.

On iPhone/iPad this only works once the app is installed to the home screen (⚙️ Settings → 📱 Install App).

🚚 Delivery Zones

Set up a fee per zone so the cashier can just pick one at checkout instead of typing a fee every time. The fee can still be typed in manually for anything unusual.

🛵 Delivery Agents

A unified list the Sales Counter picks from when assigning a delivery. Internal staff become Delivery Agents by ticking "🚚 Deliveries" under their allowed tabs in 👥 Staff Accounts — same as any other role. External riders/couriers (not on payroll, no login) are registered here instead.

Only the main branch can turn this on/off or edit these settings while it's on. When off (the default), every branch keeps its own separate logo, contact details, and paper size.

🔗 Receipt settings are managed centrally by the main branch right now — these fields are read-only here.

💳 Bill Payment Details

Shown on printed bills for customers who pay later — e.g. your Paybill/Till number and phone number. One line per detail.

📝 Receipt Notes

Extra lines printed at the bottom of every receipt and bill — e.g. "Terms and conditions apply" or "Goods once sold are not refundable." One line per statement.

📝 Hiring Counter Receipt Notes

Printed instead of the general notes above on any receipt with a hired item (Fixed Days or Count As You Go, including mixed sale+hire carts) — e.g. "Hired items must be returned in the same condition." The logo, contact details, and everything else on the receipt stay the same as the Sales Counter.

🖼️ Shop Logo on Receipts

Printed at the very top of every receipt and bill. Any PNG/JPG works — it's shrunk to thermal-printer size automatically, so a large file is fine. Thermal printers are black-and-white: a bold, high-contrast logo prints far better than a pale or detailed one.

Justified is the standard receipt table layout (item name on the left, price on the right, both edges flush). Left/Center/Right instead group each line compactly and position it at that edge. Applies to the system print dialog, the on-screen receipt, and Bluetooth/USB thermal printers alike.

📐 Paper Width

Sets the paper size for every receipt path — the system print dialog's page size, AND how many text columns are used when formatting raw ESC/POS text for Bluetooth/USB thermal printers (32 columns for 58mm, 48 for 80mm). Item names, table padding, and totals auto-adjust to match.

Most thermal printers cut automatically once the receipt is done — Auto is right for almost everyone. Only use Fixed length for pre-cut label stock or a printer that doesn't auto-cut.

Shrinks or enlarges everything on the receipt — useful if text is running slightly off the edge of your paper, or you want it more compact.

No pairing needed here — nearly all barcode scanners (USB or Bluetooth) act as a keyboard: they "type" the code and press Enter automatically. Just plug it in (or pair it as a Bluetooth keyboard in your device's Bluetooth settings), then scan.

🗄️ Cash Drawer

Cash drawers plug into the receipt printer itself (an RJ11/RJ12 port on the back), not into the computer directly — the printer sends it the "kick open" signal. Bluetooth and USB printer modes trigger this directly. "System print dialog" mode can now trigger it too, but only if your printer's driver is set to raw/"Generic / Text Only" mode (most thermal receipt printer drivers can be) — the kick command rides along inside the printed receipt itself. If your drawer doesn't open in that mode, switch the printer's driver to Generic / Text Only, or use Bluetooth/USB instead for guaranteed support.

Neither mode worked? Try raw bytes

⚠️ Danger Zone

Both actions below are permanent and cannot be undone, and both require the management password.

Permanently deletes every item in the product catalog and its stock. Sales history, hires, and staff are untouched.

Permanently removes every voided sale and voided bill from the records — they no longer show up anywhere, even struck through. Non-voided sales are untouched.

🗑️ Reset Inventory

Permanently removes every item AND service currently in Inventory, on every device. Sales history, customers, staff, and settings are not touched. A daily backup snapshot exists before this runs (see 🗄️ Backups above) in case it's a mistake.

♻️ Reset Sales & Stock History (Keep Items)

Permanently deletes every sale, bill, and stock movement record on every device — but the items themselves stay in Inventory. Any item with an opening stock recorded (see 📐 Stock Valuation on the Inventory tab) has its quantity put back to that opening figure; items with no opening stock recorded keep whatever quantity they currently have. Use "⚡ Declare All Undeclared as Opening Stock" first if you want every item to roll back cleanly. Customers, staff, expenses, and settings are not touched. This cannot be undone.

🚀 Purge Demo Data & Go Live

Been testing the app with fake sales and now ready to actually start using it? This is the same underlying reset as "Reset Sales, Keep Inventory" above, built specifically for that moment — with two extra options, a typed confirmation phrase on top of the management password, and a reminder to grab a copy of your test reports first if you want one. Your product catalog, prices, settings, staff accounts, and suppliers are never touched — only ⚠️ Reset Inventory above deletes items themselves, and that's a separate step if you want it.

🧾 Delete Voided Sales Records

A voided sale or bill is normally kept (struck-through) as an audit trail rather than deleted — see 🔒 Security & Access for how voiding itself works. This permanently ERASES every already-voided sale and bill instead of just hiding them, freeing up the list but also breaking that audit trail for good. Only sales/bills already marked voided are affected — nothing currently active is touched.

🔄 Reset App (Factory Reset)

Wipes this link back to a brand-new install — inventory, sales, customers, staff, passwords, and every setting are all cleared on every device sharing this link. Only the Business Name and Admin/Owner Name are kept, so the link itself still opens to the same shop identity, just empty. Separately-saved integrations (Payment Gateway, SMS, eTIMS, AI Capture List / Auto Product Images API keys) live outside this and are NOT cleared — turn those off individually in their own Settings sections first if you want those gone too. This cannot be undone — there is no backup restore that brings this back once it's run.

❓ Guide

Quick answers for the parts of this app that trip people up most. Tap a question to expand it.

💳 How do I get M-Pesa payments actually working?

You need one of two options, set up under ⚙️ Settings → 💳 Payment Gateway:

Option A — Paystack (simplest). Get a secret key (sk_live_... or sk_test_...) from your Paystack dashboard, paste it into "Save Paystack Key", and copy the Webhook URL shown underneath into Paystack Dashboard → Settings → API Keys & Webhooks. That's it — no Safaricom app needed.

Option B — Safaricom Daraja directly. Needs a Daraja app (Consumer Key/Secret), your Paybill or Till Number, and your Lipa Na M-Pesa Passkey. Use "Till Number" as the transaction type if you take payments on a Till, "Paybill" otherwise. The Callback URL is sent automatically with every request — you only need to copy it somewhere if Safaricom specifically asks you to pre-register one.

Once saved, the key/credential boxes disappear and are replaced with a green "✅ Payment configured" notice — that's confirmation it saved, not a sign something's hidden from you. There's no way to view a saved key again afterwards (this is deliberate, for security); to change it, use Reset to clear it and enter the new one.

If both Paystack and Daraja are configured at once, Paystack is used by default — force one specifically with the "Force a specific provider" dropdown at the bottom of that page.

🖨️ Which printer mode should I use, and why won't copies/the drawer work?

System print dialog works with any printer already installed on the device (via USB, network, or Windows/Mac driver) — no pairing needed, but it opens a print preview each time. Bluetooth and USB modes connect directly to a thermal receipt printer and print silently with no dialog at all, once paired/connected in this same Hardware settings page.

Multiple copies: set the number under "Number of Copies Printed per Receipt" — with System mode, all copies go out as ONE print job (one page per copy), so leave your printer driver's own copy count at 1 or you'll get double the copies you expect.

Cash drawer: it's the printer, not the computer, that triggers the drawer — it plugs into an RJ11/RJ12 port on the back of the printer. Bluetooth/USB modes trigger it directly. System dialog mode can too, but only if the printer's driver is set to "Generic / Text Only" (raw) mode — most thermal printer drivers support this in their settings.

Kitchen tickets use whichever printer mode is already selected here — there's currently no support for sending receipts and kitchen tickets to two different physical printers from the same device.

🖨️ How do I stop the print dialog from popping up every time?

No website or installed app — this one included — is allowed to print silently on its own. Browsers require a confirmation dialog every time; that's a security rule the browser enforces, not something any app's own code can switch off. Installing MinimartPOS to the home screen doesn't change this either.

Two real ways around it:

Bluetooth or USB thermal printer (Settings → Hardware) — these never open a dialog at all, since they send print data straight to the printer instead of going through the browser's print system. If you have a compatible thermal printer, this is the real fix.

Launch the browser with the --kiosk-printing flag — the standard trick for silent printing to a normal (non-thermal) printer via System dialog mode. Step by step:

  1. Set the printer you want to use as the Windows default printer first — Windows Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners → click it → Set as default. Kiosk-printing always uses whichever printer is currently default; there's no prompt to pick a different one.
  2. Close every open Chrome/Edge window — the flag only applies the next time the browser launches, not to a window that's already open.
  3. Find the shortcut that installing ProductionPOS created (usually the Desktop, or Start Menu → right-click ProductionPOS → "Open file location").
  4. Right-click that shortcut → Properties.
  5. Click into the Target field and go to the very end of the existing text.
  6. Type one space, then --kiosk-printing exactly (two dashes, no space inside it). It should now end with something like: ...--app-id=xxxxxxxx --kiosk-printing
  7. Click Apply, then OK.
  8. Double-click that same shortcut to reopen ProductionPOS. Printing now goes straight to the default printer with no dialog, every time.

To get the dialog back later (e.g. to pick a different printer once), remove --kiosk-printing from the Target field the same way.

📦🛠️ What's the difference between an Item and a Service?

Item — something sold exactly as it is: a bag of rice, a bar of soap. Has its own stock count and shows up in the Sales Counter.

Service — something you charge for without selling a physical unit: key cutting, delivery, installation. A plain service just has a flat price. Tick "Made from components" to link it to a bill of materials instead: add each item it uses and how much one sale uses (fractions like 1/2 work here), and the app then works out cost-per-sale and how many you can currently do from stock automatically. Tick "This is a bundle" instead to sell several items/services together (e.g. Paint + Brush + Roller) at one price — bundle components can be picked from existing stock (so their own stock is deducted correctly when it sells) or typed freely for something with nothing to track. A service is either component-based or a bundle, never both.
